primitives.name: Kalshi Anchor
primitives.verbatim_quote: MICROSTRUCTURE: Kalshi prints 0.34 on this game [docs/data-sources/research/2026-10-13/kalshi/kalshi-nfl-digest.json] -> an independent Layer-1 anchor exists beside the de-vigged book line -> when the two agree within ~2 points, the prior is solid and L2 signals apply cleanly; divergence would flag a stale book 6.
primitives.assumptions: Market efficiency underpins the Kalshi anchor; divergence between Kalshi and de-vigged book lines indicates mispricing.

layer2.mapping: The Kalshi anchor maps to a conformal prediction interval in GSI, where the observed outcome falls within the 95% credible band derived from precedent distributions.
layer2.telemetry: Track the absolute difference |P_Kalshi - P_book|; monitor for sustained deviation.

primitives.name: RYOE Adjustment
primitives.verbatim_quote: TRACKING (2026 IN-SEASON): Quinshon Judkins (CLE) records RYOE = -34.7 [docs/data-sources/research/2026-10-13/ngs/raw_statboard_rushing.json] -> live tracking proves in-season trench/separation mechanics (not historical proxy) -> provides immediate ground-truth efficiency adjustment for weekly player projections and game game-scripts 9.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'RYOE': 'Root Mean Square Error of velocity relative to reference, m²/s²', 'v_i': 'Instantaneous velocity of the running back, m/s', 'v_ref': 'Reference velocity (e.g., league average), m/s'}
primitives.assumptions: The RYOE model assumes that separation mechanics are stationary over the season and that the reference velocity captures relevant contextual factors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: RYOE > 0 indicates inefficiency; negative values suggest outperformance relative to the reference.

layer2.mapping: In GSI, RYOE feeds into a Bayesian hierarchical model that shrinks player-specific parameters toward the team mean. In GSE, it informs state-transition probabilities for downs and distances.
layer2.telemetry: Monitor rolling RYOE windows; detect shifts using changepoint detection algorithms.

primitives.name: Injury Rotation Impact
primitives.verbatim_quote: AVAILABILITY: Tylan Wallace (CLE) listed QUESTIONABLE [docs/data-sources/research/2026-10-13/injuries/espn_nfl_injuries_week6.json] -> unit rotation depth changes at that position -> snap share and pressure/scheme leverage shift toward the opponent's strength 2.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\Delta s_i': 'Change in snap share for player i, dimensionless', 'I_i': 'Binary indicator of injury for player i, {0,1}', 'S_j': 'Strength metric of opposing team j, arbitrary units'}
primitives.assumptions: The impact function f is linear; the effect scales monotonically with injury severity and opposing strength.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Large \Delta s_i occurs when high-impact players are injured against strong opponents.

layer2.mapping: This primitive maps to a conformal prediction framework where the null distribution of snap shares is conditioned on injury indicators and defensive ratings.
layer2.telemetry: Track actual snap share deviations from predicted values; use permutation tests to assess significance.

primitives.name: Precedent Coverage
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Fourth-quarter mode:** no signal - named gap: no rotation-thinning signal above threshold; late-game prop conditioning defaults to league-average fourth-quarter patterns.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Cov': 'Covariance of fourth-quarter outcomes given covariates X, arbitrary units', '\\alpha': 'League-average fourth-quarter parameter, estimated from historical data'}
primitives.assumptions: The fourth-quarter behavior is ergodic; historical averages serve as sufficient statistics for prediction.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When X is sparse (e.g., due to injuries), the coverage defaults to the unconditional mean.

layer2.mapping: In GSI, this forms a baseline predictive distribution for fourth-quarter props. In GSE, it sets transition probabilities for endgame states.
layer2.telemetry: Compare predicted fourth-quarter win probability with actual outcomes; compute calibration error.
